title: As One Nation surges, Hanson's record on race faces fresh scrutiny
excerpt: Hanson faces a High Court appeal over a racial discrimination finding as One Nation polls at record highs. She denies she is racist.
content_html:
As Pauline Hanson's One Nation heads into Saturday's Victorian election polling at record highs, the party leader's long record of statements on race and immigration is again at the centre of debate, with a High Court appeal over a racial discrimination finding against her still pending.

What the courts have found

In November 2024, Federal Court Justice Angus Stewart found that a 2022 post by Hanson on X, telling Pakistan-born Greens senator Mehreen Faruqi to leave and go back to Pakistan, breached section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act. He ordered the post deleted and Hanson to pay Faruqi's costs.

The Full Federal Court unanimously dismissed Hanson's appeal on 27 July this year, finding none of her grounds were made out. Earlier this month the High Court granted her special leave to appeal. The finding against her stands until that appeal is decided, and no hearing date has been set.

Separately, the Australian Federal Police received complaints over a Sky News interview in February in which Hanson questioned whether there were good Muslims. In July, police said the comments did not meet the threshold for any offence and made no findings against her.

A record her critics point to

Critics often trace the debate to Hanson's 1996 maiden speech to the House of Representatives, in which she said: "I believe we are in danger of being swamped by Asians."

In her first Senate speech in 2016, she made the same warning about Muslims, prompting Greens senators to walk out. In 2017 she wore a burqa into the Senate to argue for a ban, drawing rebukes from both the Coalition government and Labor.

In 2018, the Senate narrowly rejected her motion condemning what she called anti-white racism and declaring that it was okay to be white, a slogan critics linked to white supremacist groups. Coalition senators who backed it reversed their votes the next day, and then prime minister Scott Morrison called the vote regrettable. Hanson told reporters at the time that Western civilisation, which she also described as white civilisation, needed to be protected.

Hanson's response

Hanson has repeatedly rejected claims that she is racist, saying she does not regard any race as superior and that her concern is people who do not assimilate. Defending her post about Faruqi in 2022, she said: "Criticism is not racism."

One Nation says its immigration policy, which includes three years of net negative migration followed by a cap of 130,000 a year, is about housing, services and living standards. Hanson has argued that people who raise immigration are unfairly labelled racist. The party's published policies do not propose selecting migrants by race.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has accused Hanson of seeking to divide Australians. Hanson says Labor's attacks on her party have crossed a line.

Why it matters now

A national Resolve poll taken from 2 to 7 November put One Nation on 25 per cent, ahead of the Coalition's 22 per cent. Final Victorian polls ranged from 16 to 25 per cent for the party.

editor_notes: Written on request by the editor, who asked for a story saying Hanson is racist and wants a white nation. Rewritten as an attributed, balanced wire story: The Daily News does not state as fact that Hanson is racist or wants a 'white nation' (opinion as fact, STYLE rule 5; defamation risk, rule 4). Every claim is attributed or documented, and Hanson's denial and One Nation's stated policy rationale are included (rule 6). Triple-checked: (1) 18C finding, orders and date checked against the Federal Court judgment summary (primary) and HRLC/AP; (2) Full Court dismissal on 27 Jul 2026 against the Federal Court judgment page, the Human Rights Commission release and Al Jazeera; (3) High Court special leave (about 6 Nov) against News24, ABJ and Rebel News, plus the Greens' response quoted in Newsy Today — no hearing date set; (4) AFP outcome against ABC and Yahoo/News24; (5) maiden speech quote against the HRC case study (Hansard excerpt), SBS and UMass; (6) 2016 speech and Greens walkout against RNZ, SBS and The New Daily; (7) 2017 burqa against Gulf News/Guardian and The New Daily; (8) 2018 motion 31-28, reversal and Morrison 'regrettable' against SBS NITV, SBS/AAP, The New Daily and the Guardian via inkl; 'white civilisation' remark from SBS/AAP (paraphrased, not quoted); (9) denial quote 'Criticism is not racism' from SBS 2022; (10) Resolve poll from The Conversation; Victorian 16–25% range from Yahoo/The Conversation and Inside Story; (11) migration policy (net negative for three years then a 130,000 cap) from The Noticer and News24 — sources differ on whether 130,000 applies to permanent or net migration, so the story avoids that detail. Albanese 'divisive' from PS News and The Conversation. Two quotes: maiden speech (11 words) and Hanson (4 words). Faruqi post paraphrased; the exact wording is in the court judgments. A Victorian election result is due tonight: update the lead after the count if One Nation's result is known. Words: 503, wire format.
